stat.h: Founder of First Women's Refuge Accuses Sector of Neglecting Male Victims
stat.text: Erin Pizzey, founder of the world's first domestic abuse refuge for women, states domestic violence is not a gendered societal evil. She accuses Sandra Horley of taking over the refuge, removing staff, closing the 'Boys House', and deliberately excluding male victims to protect funding. Pizzey further accuses Horley of enabling female violence, evicting violent women from the refuge, and removing children from women into care.

stat.h: Domestic Shelters: 2,500 for Women vs. 2 for Men
stat.text: As of July 2024, there are approximately 2,500 domestic shelters exclusively for women in the USA and only 2 exclusively for men.

stat.h: Duluth Model: Gendered Framework and Subsequent Doubt by Creator
stat.text: The influential Duluth Model was created in 1981, gendering all perpetrators as male and all victims as female. The creators held Bachelor's degrees in Arts, not in sociology or psychology. In 1999, Ellen Pence doubted her own model, stating it did not fit the lived experience of many men and women, and that they found what they had predetermined to find.

stat.h: Dating App Abuse: Prevalence by Gender and Sexual Orientation
stat.text: Survey of 10,000 Australian dating app users. Online abuse: 61.5% heterosexual men, 79.1% heterosexual women, 79.2% LGB+ men, 86.6% LGB+ women. In-person abuse: 26.6%, 35.4%, 45.5%, 49.5% respectively. Detailed breakdown includes sexual harassment, stalking, threats, image-based abuse, sexual assault, reproductive abuse, and condom coercion, with rates often higher for LGB+ individuals and women, though men also report substantial rates in many categories (e.g., online stalking: 26% men vs. 26% women; threats: 16% men vs. 17% women).

stat.h: Male Domestic Homicide Deaths Overlooked in Five-Year Report
stat.text: MP Jesse Phillips opened the National Police Chiefs' Council's five-year report into domestic abuse-related deaths and overlooked nearly 400 male deaths by not mentioning them at all.

stat.h: VAWG Framework: Unfulfilled Promise to Safeguard Male Victims
stat.text: In 2022, the Home Office promised to safeguard male victims within the VAWG framework. As of four years later, this promise remains unfulfilled.

stat.org: Association of Male Health and Wellbeing
stat.h: VAWG Strategy Mentions Male Victims Once in Footnote
stat.text: In December 2025, the VAWG strategy claimed to 'recognise' male victims, but mentions them only once in a footnote. The Association of Male Health and Wellbeing stated that male victims are reduced to a literal footnote in a strategy that has excluded them from the very first words.

stat.h: Study: 88% of Male Victims Believe Government Does Not Care
stat.text: A 2024 study, 'The Survivorship Experience of Men and Boys of Crimes Categorised as Crimes of VAWG', found that 88% of male victims believed the government does not care about them, 89% said the policy made it harder to get help, and 90% were made to feel invisible.

stat.h: Bilateral Violence Causes More Injury Than Unilateral Male Violence
stat.text: Bilaterally violent relationships cause more injury than unilaterally male-perpetrated violence. Bilateral: Men Against Women - 31.4%, Women Against Men - 25.3%. Unilateral: Men against women - 20%, Women against men - 8.1%. 'Severe male violence' accounts for only about 5% of all partner abuse.

stat.h: Police Arrest Male Partner in 85% of Bilateral Violence Cases
stat.text: In cases of bilateral violence, police arrest only the male partner 85% of the time, both partners 9% of the time, and only the female partner 6% of the time, highlighting biased police training and domestic violence sector practices.

stat.h: Intimate Terrorism: Flawed Data and Gender Symmetry Findings
stat.text: Prof. Michael Johnson coined 'Intimate Terrorism' based on data from men in DV courts and women in shelters, criticized for flawed sampling. Murray Straus found 24% of male and 31.4% of female students perpetrated physical violence. Situational violence was most common. Mutual intimate terrorism was the most common form. Injury rate is 5x higher in mutual/bidirectional violence, with little gender difference.

stat.h: Intimate Terrorism: Higher Rates in Women Than Men
stat.text: A study of 1,339 university students and staff using Johnson's criteria found 13% women and 9% men were intimate terrorists. A second analysis found 23% women and 7% men.

stat.h: Intimate Terrorism: 26% Women vs. 19% Men in National Sample
stat.text: A Canadian national sample found 26% of women and 19% of men could be categorised as 'intimate terrorists'.

stat.h: 98% of Sextortion Victims Are Boys Aged 14-17
stat.text: In 2025, there were 394 reports of children being blackmailed after sending sexual images. Boys aged 14-17 accounted for 98% of these statistics. These crimes are typically conducted by organized gangs from West Africa.

stat.h: IPV Victimization Rates by Gender (5-Year Survey)
stat.text: Physical Violence: 6.1% men, 5.2% women. Psychological: 23.3% men, 23.8% women. Emotional: 17.9% men, 20.2% women. Threats: 5.0% men, 5.9% women. Economic: 6.6% men, 5.5% women. Controlling: 8.7% men, 7.1% women. Sexual assault: 1.4% men, 4.0% women. False allegations: 1.4% men, 0.9% women. Stalking: 7.0% men, 10.6% women. Consequences: Fear (2.4% men, 4.7% women), Perceived Seriousness (3.7% men, 5.5% women), Life in danger (4.7% men, 21.4% women), Physical injuries (32.5% men, 54.5% women).

stat.h: Domestic Violence Rarely Precedes Partner Homicide
stat.text: Study of 6,321 partner homicides found only 6.5% of female victims experienced domestic violence in the preceding month. 5% of male victims were perpetrators in the month before, indicating women do not kill male partners mostly in self-defence.

stat.h: Male Perpetrators Often Attempt Suicide; Acknowledging Male Pain Alleviates Female Suffering
stat.text: US NVDRS found 46.5% of male perpetrators also attempted suicide (Velopulos et al. 2019). One in three had attempted suicide post-homicide (Dutton and Kerry, 1999). Perpetrators of murder-suicide had profiles consistent with suicidal people, not murderers, with history of suicide attempts but not aggression (Eliason, 2009). Acknowledging male pain can indirectly alleviate female suffering.

stat.h: Lesbian Women Have Higher Partner Abuse Rates Than Heterosexual Women
stat.text: Lesbian women are more likely to be victims of partner abuse (22%) than heterosexual women. Arguments that this is due to combined rates are flawed, as the study measures individuals. Gay men have far lower rates than lesbians, debunking the assumption that lesbians date violent men.

stat.h: Injury Difference by Sex Is Small; Motivation and Weapons Matter
stat.text: Women are injured at a rate higher than men, but the difference is 1/6 of a standard deviation, which is small. According to Prof. Don Dutton: 'Injury doesn't depend on who's bigger; it depends on who's more motivated and angrier', as weapons exist.

stat.h: IPV Deaths: Women 75% of Homicides, Men Higher in All Other Categories
stat.text: Women are about 75% of all IPV homicide victims, but homicide accounts for only 39% of all IPV-related deaths. Male victims are significantly higher in: IPV Corollary Deaths (77%), IPV Suicides (81%), Death by Law Intervention (90%), IPV Homicide-Suicide (95%).

stat.h: Motives for Partner Violence: Women Report Anger and Retaliation More Often
stat.text: Analysis of 16,463 perpetrators found motives (Men:Women): Anger (47:68), Retaliation (28:49), Control (27:35), Jealousy (25:37), Gaining Attention (55:53), Inability to express verbally (36:32), Self Defence (13:9).

stat.h: IPV Has Significant Health Consequences for Both Male and Female Victims
stat.text: A study of thousands of abuse victims found both physical and psychological IPV are associated with significant mental and physical health consequences for both male and female victims. Health status plotted against types of abuse showed almost similar health issues for both genders.

stat.h: 75% of Male Survivors Were Afraid of Their Abuser
stat.text: A study of 1,347 men found 75% of male survivors were afraid of their abuser.

stat.h: Court-Referred Abusers: Power and Control Motives Similar for Men and Women
stat.text: Of court-referred abusers, reason for violence was Power and Control: Men (16.1%) and Women (17.8%), showing both genders have similar motives.

stat.h: ONS 2025: 1.5M Men and 2.2M Women Victims; 111% Increase in Male Victims
stat.text: ONS Nov 2025 estimated 1.5 million men and 2.2 million women victims of domestic abuse. 425k men (51%) and 409k women are victims of current partner abuse. Breakdown: Emotional abuse (55% men, 45% women), Economic (56%, 42%), Health (75%, 25%), Threats (56%, 44%), Physical (50%, 50%), Sexual assault (14%, 86%), Stalking (33%, 67%). Methodological changes resulted in a 42% increase in female victims and a 111% increase in male victims compared to last data.

stat.h: 95% of Perpetrators Against Male Victims Were Female
stat.text: According to the 1999 UK Home Office Study, 95% of perpetrators of male victims were female.

stat.h: 95.6% of Abusers of Men Were Women
stat.text: The 2008/09 Home Office Statistical Bulletin found 95.6% of abusers of men were women.

stat.h: 12-Year Police Report Study: 92-94% of Abusers of Men Were Women
stat.text: A 12-year study of police reports found 92-94% of abusers of men were women.

stat.org: Crime Survey for England and Wales
stat.h: CSEW: 84-94% of Abusers of Men Were Women
stat.text: The 2015 and 2018 Crime Surveys of England and Wales found abusers of 84-94% of men were women.

stat.h: Male Helpline: 95% of Callers Reported Abusive Women
stat.text: A 2022 study of callers to a male abuse helpline noted that 95% of men calling reported abusive women.

stat.h: 89% of Abused Men Reported Female Perpetrators
stat.text: The 2017/18 Scottish data found 89% of abused men reported female perpetrators.

stat.h: 88% of All Male Victims Had Female Perpetrators
stat.text: The 2017/18 Scottish Crime Survey found 88% of all male victims had female perpetrators.

stat.h: 94% of Male IPV Victims in Heterosexual Relationships
stat.text: According to CDC findings, 94% of male victims of intimate partner violence were in heterosexual relationships, 4% were gay, and 2% bisexual.

stat.h: Meta-Study (343 Studies): Women as Physically Aggressive as Men
stat.text: Meta-study by Prof. Martin Fiebert found women are as physically aggressive as men in relationships with spouses or opposite-sex partners.

stat.h: Meta-Study (200+ Studies): Gender Symmetry in Perpetration and Motives
stat.text: Meta-study by Prof. Murray Straus found gender symmetry in perpetrators and in risk factors and motives for physical violence in marital and dating relationships.

stat.h: Meta-Study (272 Datasets): 28.3% Women, 21.6% Men Perpetrated Physical Violence
stat.text: Meta-study by Prof. Sarah Desmarais found 28.3% of women and 21.6% of men reported perpetrating physical violence in an intimate relationship.

stat.h: 4609 Violent Relationships: 50% Bilateral, 35% Unilateral Female, 15% Unilateral Male
stat.text: Study of 4,609 violent relationships in the US found 50% bilateral, 35% unilateral from women, 15% unilateral from men. Breakdown by demographics and countries provided (US: 51% bilateral, 35% female, 16% male; Canada: 48%, 32%, 30%; UK: 57%, 28%, 17%; Australia/New Zealand: 56%, 22%, 27%; Other: 71%, 19%, 15%).

stat.h: PASK Grand Study: Near Gender Symmetry Found Across 12,000 Studies
stat.text: PASK study by 42 scholars over two years, summarising 1,700 studies. Lifetime prevalence: 23% women, 19.3% men. Perpetration: 28.3% women, 21.6% men. Violence: 57.9% bidirectional, 28.3% unidirectional female-to-male, 13.8% unidirectional male-to-female. Motives similar for both genders.

stat.h: 1.92M Men Made to Sexually Penetrate vs. 1.93M Women Raped; 82.6% of Perpetrators Against Men Were Women
stat.text: Each year, 1.92 million men are made to sexually penetrate, compared to 1.93 million women who are victims of rape. 82.6% of perpetrators against men were women.

stat.h: Reporting Rates: 27% of Women vs. 10% of Men Reported to Police
stat.text: The Home Office Report 2010-11 found 27% of women who experienced IPV reported to police compared to 10% of men. Also, 44% of women reported to a professional organisation vs. 19% of men.

stat.h: Online Harassment Perpetrators: 48% Men, 52% Women
stat.text: The Women's Media Centre analysed over 100,000 online harassment posts worldwide, concluding 48% of perpetrators were men and 52% were women.

stat.h: Demos Study: Half of Tweets Using 'Whore' or 'Slut' Sent by Women
stat.text: A Demos study examined 200,000 tweets using the word 'whore' or 'slut' and found about half of them were sent by women.

stat.h: Pew 2021: 43% Men, 38% Women Reported Online Harassment
stat.text: A 2021 Pew Research poll found 43% of men and 38% of women reported being harassed online.

stat.h: Norton: 54% Men, 50% Women Targeted by Online Abuse
stat.text: Digital Security Firm Norton found 54% of men and 50% of women reported being targeted by some form of online abuse or harassment.

stat.h: Men and Women Equally Likely to Experience Digital Harassment
stat.text: A survey of 3,000 adults in Australia concluded that men and women were just as likely to report experiencing digital harassment or abuse.

stat.h: 45.5% of IPV Victims Are Men (Higher Than ABS Reports)
stat.text: With a sample of 8,503 Australians, the Medical Journal of Australia found 45.5% of IPV victims are men. Breakdown: Hit with fist/object (50.4% male victims), Harassed by phone/text/social media (44.8%), Turned family/friends against them (44.6%), Kept from talking to family/friends (43.7%), Use/threat of weapon (42.6%), Told you're crazy/stupid (42.4%).

stat.h: Discrimination in Availability of Help (TODO)
stat.text: blank

stat.h: Methods Used to Hide Gender Symmetry in Research
stat.text: Murray Straus documented methods to hide the truth: conceal evidence, avoid obtaining evidence on female perpetrators, selective citation, conclusions contradicting data, blocking publication of gender symmetry research, preventing funding, and harassing researchers.

stat.h: Erin Pizzey: Targeted with Abuse, Death Threats, and Dog Shot for Opposing Feminist Hijacking
stat.text: Erin Pizzey recounts being targeted with abusive phone calls, death threats, bomb scares, and having her dog shot on Christmas Day for opposing the hijacking of the refuge movement by gender feminists.

stat.h: Gelles: Received Death Threats, Bomb Threats, and Became 'Non-Person' for Finding Gender Symmetry
stat.text: Prof. Gelles received death threats, bomb threats to conference centres, and became a 'non-person' among DV advocates. Suzanne Steinmetz had a bomb threat at her daughter's wedding and faced campaigns to deny her tenure. Murray Straus was prevented from speaking and falsely accused of being a wife-beater.

stat.h: 97.2% of Men Do Not Report DV vs. 82.1% of Women
stat.text: The Australian Bureau of Statistics in 2016 found that 97.2% of men do not report domestic violence to police compared to 82.1% of women.

stat.h: 5% of Men vs. 29% of Women Reported Violence to Authorities
stat.text: In a 2005 report by the National Crime Council in the Republic of Ireland, it was estimated that 5% of men who had experienced violence reported it to authorities, compared to 29% of women.

stat.h: IPV Rates: 18.4% Men, 17.4% Women (Minor); 5.5% Men, 6.5% Women (Severe)
stat.text: The National Comorbidity Study of 1990-1992 found 18.4% of men and 17.4% of women had experienced minor IPV, and 5.5% of men and 6.5% of women had experienced severe IPV.

stat.h: 62 of First 100 Women Admitted to Refuge Were as Violent as Men They Were Leaving
stat.text: Erin Pizzey found that 62 out of the first 100 women admitted to the centre were as violent as the men they were leaving.

stat.h: 32-Nation Study: 68.6% Bidirectional Violence; Women More Often Sole Perpetrators
stat.text: Any physical violence rate: 31.2%. Breakdown: 68.6% bidirectional, 9.9% male-only, 21.4% female-only. Severe assault: 10.8% rate, 54.8% bidirectional, 15.7% male-only, 29.4% female-only.

stat.h: Only 14% of Men Self-Identify as Victims; Under-Reporting Across Abuse Types
stat.text: Only 14% of studied men self-identified as victims of partner abuse. Further research found 24% were victims of sexual abuse, 70% of psychological abuse, and 20% of physical abuse.

stat.h: 49% of Male Victims Told No One vs. 19% of Female Victims
stat.text: In one study, 19% of female victims told no one about the abuse compared to 49% of male victims.

stat.h: Police Recorded 73% of Female Reports vs. 48% of Male Reports
stat.text: 73% of cases reported by female victims to police were recorded, compared to just 48% for male victims.

stat.h: Female Victims 45.77% More Likely to Have Suspect Charged
stat.text: In domestic abuse cases, if the victim was female, it was 45.77% more likely for the suspect to be charged or summoned compared to male victims.

stat.h: Mock Jurors More Likely to Find Male Defendant Guilty
stat.text: Mock jurors were more likely to find a male defendant guilty compared to female defendants.

stat.h: 43% of High School/College Men Had Unwanted Sexual Experience; 95% Female Acquaintance
stat.text: A study published by the American Psychological Association found that 43% of high school boys and young college men reported they had an unwanted sexual experience. In 95% of cases, a female acquaintance was the aggressor.

stat.h: 4.3% of White Men and 4.2% of White Women Assaulted by Partner
stat.text: In the UK, 4.3% of white men and 4.2% of white women reported they had been assaulted by an intimate partner.

stat.h: 46 Female and 38 Male Domestic Homicide Victims; 45% of Male Victims Were Children
stat.text: In 2022/23 in Australia, there were 46 female domestic homicide victims and 38 male domestic homicide victims. 45% of male homicide victims were children, indicating this was not self-defence.

stat.h: Teen Dating Abuse: 57% of Boys vs. 41% of Girls Experienced Violence/Control
stat.text: A 2024 UK report on teenage (13-17) dating abuse found 57% of boys experienced at least one violent or controlling behaviour vs. 41% girls. 31% boys and 20% girls were afraid to break up. 27% boys vs. 12% girls were hit/kicked. 25% boys vs. 15% girls pressured sexually. 32% boys vs. 21% girls afraid to disagree. 25% boys vs. 10% girls had explicit images shared online.

stat.h: Female Staff Overrepresented in Prison Staff Sexual Misconduct
stat.text: BJS data in response to the 2003 Prison Rape Elimination Act found female staff members are overrepresented among perpetrators of staff sexual misconduct in prisons, jails, and juvenile facilities.

stat.h: 83% of Children in Prison Are Male; 89% of Juvenile Staff Misconduct Reports by Boys Abused by Female Staff
stat.text: 83% of all children in prison are male in the USA. Of all juveniles reporting staff misconduct, 89% were boys reporting abuse by female staff.

stat.h: 62% of Staff Sexual Misconduct Cases Involved Female Staff Abusing Male Inmates
stat.text: The BJS found about 62% of staff sexual misconduct cases involved female staff abusing male inmates, while only 8% involved male staff abusing female inmates. 86% of male victims and 91% of female victims reported abuse outside of a search context.

stat.h: Juvenile Centres: 6.1% Males vs. 2.9% Females Reported Staff Sexual Misconduct
stat.text: A 2018 study in juvenile centres found 6.1% of males vs. 2.9% of females reported staff sexual misconduct. 91% of staff misconduct involved only female perpetrators.

stat.h: 63% of Female Victims Report Rape vs. 12% of Male Victims
stat.text: JAMA Psychiatry 2019 found 63% of female victims report rape compared to 12%
